purpose: Skeleton-first metacarpal/phalange target constraints to be applied after canonical carpal centroids and CMC contacts are solved.

M1.reason: a003 48 mm is inside 46±3 mm male radiographic band; no second numeric source registered.

M2.reason: 68 mm radiographic mean and 67.7 mm CT mean independently converge; a003 is ~9-10 mm shorter.

M3.reason: 64 mm radiographic mean and 66.1 mm CT mean converge on a substantially longer bone; a003 is ~10-12 mm shorter.

M4.reason: both sources give ~58 mm; a003 ~51.6 mm is below the 1-SD male band.

M5.reason: 54 mm radiographic and 52.3 mm CT means bracket a003 ~53.2 mm.

provisional_length_corridors_mm.note: These are evidence corridors, not frozen exact targets. M2-M4 should move into corridor only after CMC positions are solved from canonical carpal geometry.

phalange_policy.reason: Most a003 digit phalange spans are within 2 SD of the registered male radiographic sample; no gross chain defect comparable with M2-M4 is established.
requirements: preserve digit-specific proximal/middle/distal ratios rather than uniform finger recipes
keep thumb as two phalanges and digits 2-5 as three
distal phalanx tip must separate bone endpoint from soft-tissue fingertip allowance

geometric_rules: Metacarpal length means CMC/base-to-MCP/head compatible span; do not add carpal length into the metacarpal target.
MCP centres must be derived from canonical CMC contacts plus ray direction and selected metacarpal length—not from the old short mesh stations.
Finger phalange chains start from the rebuilt MCP centres; do not move canonical MCP centres back to fit the current r95 hand.
The final hand skin length is checked only after carpal + metacarpal + phalange chain and explicit fingertip soft-tissue allowance are assembled.
implementation_order: select metacarpal lengths inside evidence corridors
derive MCP centres and palm arch
attach provisionally retained phalange chains and recheck ratios
